q: How does the IRR define a 'Foreign Architect'?
o: An architect who is not a Filipino citizen nor registered/licensed in the Philippines, but is duly registered and licensed as an architect in his/her home country
A Filipino architect who works overseas
Any non-citizen employee of an architectural firm
Any architect who studied outside the Philippines, regardless of citizenship
Hindi po alam
n: Section 3(30) defines 'Foreign Architect' as an architect who is not a Filipino citizen nor an architect registered and licensed in the Philippines, but who is duly registered and licensed in his/her home country as an architect. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(30))

q: Per Section 34, can a non-registered person describe his/her services as equivalent to a registered architect's, so long as the title 'Architect' is never actually used?
o: Yes, as long as the word 'Architect' itself is avoided
No — non-registered persons may not claim or represent their services as equivalent to a registered architect's, even without using the title
Yes, provided they hold a civil engineering license instead
Yes, if they have more than ten years of informal experience
n: Section 34 states that non-registered persons shall not claim or represent their services or work as equivalent to those of a duly registered architect, or that they are qualified for any branch of architectural practice, even without using the title. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 34)

q: Once issued upon payment of the annual registration fee, how long does a Professional Identification Card (PIC) remain valid before renewal is due?
o: One (1) year
Two (2) years
Three (3) years
Five (5) years
n: Section 3(37) defines the Professional Identification Card as bearing a registration number and expiry date, issued upon payment of the annual registration fees for three (3) years. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(37))

q: Under Section 35(3), what percentage of project cost may a government architect-of-record collect as incentive pay for civil liabilities, and what cap applies against his/her annual salary?
o: 0.5% of project cost, with no cap
10% of project cost, not exceeding 25% of annual salary
5% of project cost, not exceeding 100% of annual salary
1.5% of project cost, not exceeding 50% of annual salary
n: Section 35(3) provides an incentive pay equivalent to 1.5% of the project cost, provided it shall not exceed 50% of the government architect's annual salary, payable upon full completion of the project. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 35(3))

q: What does the acronym CIAC stand for?
o: Construction Industry Arbitration Commission
Philippine Contractors Accreditation Board
Commission on Higher Education
Professional Disciplinary Compliance Board
n: Section 3(45) lists CIAC as the acronym for the Construction Industry Arbitration Commission. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(45)(d))

q: Government architect Dela Cruz earns an annual salary of P600,000 and serves as architect-of-record for an P8,000,000 project. Applying the 1.5% incentive-pay rule under Section 35(3), subject to the 50%-of-salary cap, how much incentive pay is she entitled to?
o: P600,000 (100% of her annual salary)
P120,000 (1.5% of project cost, which is below the P300,000 cap, so the full amount is paid)
P8,000 flat fee
P300,000 (the salary cap applies regardless)
n: 1.5% of the P8,000,000 project cost is P120,000. The 50%-of-salary cap is 50% of P600,000 = P300,000. Since P120,000 is below the cap, the full 1.5% computed amount (P120,000) is paid, not the cap. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 35(3) (applied computation))

q: How is the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture (the 'Board') made up?
o: Five (5) members elected by all registered architects
Seven (7) members appointed by the Department of Trade and Industry
A chairman and two (2) members appointed by the President of the Philippines
A chairman appointed by the PRC Chairperson alone, with no other members
n: Section 4 provides that the Board is composed of a chairman and two (2) members appointed by the President of the Philippines from a list of recommendees submitted by the integrated and accredited professional organization of architects. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule II, Sec. 4)

q: Per Section 36, is it lawful for someone who isn't a registered architect to collect a fee for architectural services?
o: Yes, if the fee is below the Standards of Professional Practice minimum
Yes, if disclosed to the client in writing
Yes, without restriction
It is unlawful, except when acting as an employee collecting a fee as representative of a Registered Architect
n: Section 36 makes it unlawful for an unregistered person to collect a fee for architectural services, except as an employee collecting on behalf of, and as a representative of, a Registered Architect. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 36)

q: The Board must be organized within what period from the effectivity of the Architecture Act of 2004?
o: Six (6) months
Thirty (30) days
Sixty (60) days
One (1) year
n: Section 4 states the Board shall be organized not later than six (6) months from the effectivity of the Architecture Act of 2004. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule II, Sec. 4)

q: Under Section 37(a), who is permitted to form and register an architectural firm, company, partnership, association, or corporation, whether alone or with allied technical professionals?
o: Any civil engineer, with or without an architecture license
Only Filipino citizens properly registered and licensed as architects under R.A. No. 9266
Any DTI-registered business owner
Any foreign national residing in the Philippines
n: Section 37(a) provides that only Filipino citizens properly registered and licensed as architects under R.A. No. 9266 may, among themselves or with allied technical professionals, form and register such an entity. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 37(a))

q: A former faculty member of a school teaching architecture may qualify for the Board only after having fully ceased teaching, advising, or reviewing activities for at least how long before nomination?
o: One (1) year
Three (3) years
Five (5) years
Ten (10) years
n: Section 5(d) requires that a former faculty member must have officially resigned and completely stopped teaching, advising or reviewing activities for at least five (5) years prior to nomination in order to qualify for the Board. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule II, Sec. 5(d))

q: Per Section 38's procedure, within how many calendar days from a foreign architect's commission/appointment date must the commissioning party obtain his/her Temporary/Special Permit?
o: Sixty (60) calendar days
Ninety (90) calendar days
Fifteen (15) calendar days
Thirty (30) calendar days
n: Section 38, sub-rule 2.0, requires the commissioning party to secure the Temporary/Special Permit from the Board (subject to PRC approval) within thirty (30) calendar days after the commission/appointment date. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 38 (sub-rule 2.0))

q: For the very first Board appointed under R.A. No. 9266, how were the chairman's and members' initial terms staggered?
o: One member for three (3) years, one for two (2) years, one for one (1) year
All three served three (3) years
All three served one (1) year only
The chairman served six (6) years, members served three (3) years
n: Section 6 provides that of the members first appointed, one shall hold office as chairman for three years, one member for two years, and one member for one year. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule II, Sec. 6)

q: Section 39 gave the Board how many months from R.A. No. 9266's effectivity to implement rules on professional liability/malpractice insurance for foreign nationals under a temporary/special permit?
o: Three (3) months
Six (6) months
One (1) year
Two (2) years
n: Section 39 required the Board, in consultation with the integrated and accredited professional organization, to implement the liability/malpractice insurance requirement within six (6) months from the effectivity of R.A. No. 9266. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 39)

q: As originally provided in this IRR, does Section 7(i) make CPD attendance mandatory for renewing a Professional Identification Card?
o: Only architects over 60 years old are exempted
Only foreign architects are exempted
No, attendance to CPD shall not be a mandatory requirement for PIC renewal
Yes, it is an absolute mandatory requirement
n: Section 7(i) states that the Board shall prescribe CPD guidelines, provided that attendance to said CPD shall not be a mandatory requirement for the renewal of a Professional Identification Card. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule II, Sec. 7(i))

q: Does belonging to the integrated and accredited professional organization of architects (UAP) stop an architect from also joining other architects' associations?
o: Yes, membership is exclusive and bars any other association membership
Only architects who are Board members may join other associations
Only foreign architects may join other associations
No — membership in the IAPOA/UAP shall not be a bar to membership in other associations of architects
n: Section 40 explicitly states that membership in the integrated and accredited professional organization of architects shall not be a bar to membership in other voluntary associations of architects. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule V, Sec. 40)

q: The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture operates under whose administrative supervision, and who keeps custody of its exam and case records?
o: The Professional Regulation Commission; records under the custody of the Commission
The Office of the President; records kept by Malacañang
The Department of Trade and Industry; records kept by the Board itself
The United Architects of the Philippines; records kept by UAP
n: Section 8 states the Board is under the administrative supervision of the Commission, and all records — applications, exam questions, answer sheets, case records — are under the custody of the Commission. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule II, Sec. 8)

q: Section 41 required the Board to adopt and promulgate the IRR, Code of Ethical Conduct, and Standards of Professional Practice within how many days of R.A. No. 9266's effectivity?
o: Thirty (30) days
Sixty (60) days
Ninety (90) days
Fifteen (15) days
n: Section 41 required the Board, subject to Commission approval and in coordination with the integrated and accredited professional organization, to adopt and promulgate the IRR, Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice within sixty (60) days after the effectivity of R.A. No. 9266. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule V, Sec. 41)

q: Who is empowered to suspend or remove a Board member, and based on whose recommendation?
o: The Senate, on recommendation of the House of Representatives
The Ombudsman, motu proprio
The President of the Philippines, upon recommendation of the Commission, after due administrative investigation
The UAP Board of Directors, without need for investigation
n: Section 9 provides that the President of the Philippines, upon the recommendation of the Commission, after giving the member an opportunity to be heard in an administrative investigation, may suspend or remove a Board member. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule II, Sec. 9)

q: Per Section 42, whose annual budget — through the General Appropriations Act — funds the implementation of R.A. No. 9266?
o: The United Architects of the Philippines
The Department of Public Works and Highways
The Department of Trade and Industry
The Professional Regulation Commission
n: Section 42 states the Chairperson of the PRC shall include in the Commission's programs the implementation of R.A. No. 9266, funded through the annual General Appropriations Act. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule V, Sec. 42)

q: Beyond a BS Architecture degree and good moral character, what practical requirement does Section 13 impose on an examination applicant?
o: At least two (2) years or equivalent of diversified architectural experience duly certified by a registered/licensed architect
Passing a preliminary aptitude test administered by UAP
At least five (5) years of diversified architectural experience
Completion of a master's degree in architecture
n: Section 13(c) requires a specific record of at least two (2) years or equivalent of diversified architectural experience, duly certified by a registered/licensed architect. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 13(c))

q: Under Section 44, who besides the Commission and Board is tasked to act as legal adviser and provide legal assistance in enforcing R.A. No. 9266?
o: The Solicitor General exclusively
The Secretary of Justice or his/her duly designated representative
The Ombudsman
The Commission on Audit
n: Section 44 provides that the Secretary of Justice or his duly designated representative shall act as legal adviser to the Commission and Board and render legal assistance in enforcing the law. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule V, Sec. 44)

q: An applicant with a BS in Architecture plus a Master's Degree from a recognized institution has logged only eight (8) months of actual diversified experience. Given the two-year base requirement and the one-year credit for the Master's degree, how many more months must this applicant complete to qualify for the licensure exam?
o: 16 months
8 months
4 months
12 months
n: The base requirement is 2 years (24 months); the Master's degree credits 1 year (12 months), leaving a net requirement of 12 months. The applicant has already completed 8 months, so 12 - 8 = 4 more months are needed. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 13(c) (applied computation))

q: Section 46 (Repealing Clause) expressly identifies which prior laws/issuances as superseded or repealed to the extent inconsistent with the IRR?
o: The National Building Code (P.D. 1096) in its entirety
The Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines (R.A. No. 8293)
The Local Government Code of 1991
R.A. No. 545 (as amended by R.A. No. 1581), P.D. No. 223 (as amended), and R.A. No. 8981
n: Section 46 states that provisions of rules, regulations, codes, orders and policies issued pursuant to R.A. No. 545 (as amended by R.A. No. 1581), P.D. No. 223 (as amended), R.A. No. 8981, and other inconsistent laws are superseded, repealed or amended. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule V, Sec. 46)

q: What may the Board do, under Section 13, if an examination or registration application involves false evidence, misrepresentation, or false swearing?
o: Refuse to renew a professional identification card, or suspend/revoke a certificate, or refuse to renew or grant registration
Nothing; the Board has no power to act on false applications
Transfer jurisdiction to the Department of Justice exclusively
Automatically imprison the applicant without a hearing
n: Section 13 provides the Board may refuse to renew a PIC, or suspend or revoke a certificate of registration obtained by false swearing or misrepresentation, and may refuse to renew or grant registration to an applicant whose application contains false evidence. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 13)

q: How does the document titled 'IRR of the Architecture Act of 2004' relate overall to Republic Act No. 9266?
o: The IRR repeals R.A. No. 9266 in its entirety
The IRR is the set of Implementing Rules and Regulations promulgated by the Board of Architecture (per Sec. 7(a) and Sec. 41, Art. V of R.A. 9266) to carry out R.A. No. 9266's provisions
R.A. No. 9266 is a mere draft version of the IRR
They are entirely separate and unrelated laws
n: The IRR's preamble states it was promulgated by the Board of Architecture pursuant to Sec. 7(a), Article II, and Sec. 41, Article V of R.A. No. 9266 to carry out that law's provisions. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Preamble)

q: Who may revise, drop, or add examination subjects and syllabi to keep pace with technological change, and whose approval must this have?
o: The UAP alone, without Board approval
CHED, without consulting the Board
The Board, subject to the approval of the Commission
Individual review centers, at their discretion
n: Section 14 provides that the Board, subject to the approval of the Commission, may revise or exclude any of the subjects and their syllabi, and add new ones as the need arises. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 14)

q: In total, how many Rules make up the IRR of the Architecture Act of 2004?
o: Three (3) Rules
Four (4) Rules
Seven (7) Rules
Five (5) Rules
n: The IRR is organized into five Rules: Rule I (Title/Definitions/Scope), Rule II (Board Organization), Rule III (Examination/Registration/Licensure), Rule IV (Practice of Architecture), and Rule V (Final Provisions). (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rules I-V)

q: Candidate A scores 78%, 74%, 68%, and 82% across four subjects in the licensure exam, giving a weighted general average of 75.5%. Does Candidate A pass under Section 15?
o: Yes — the weighted average (75.5%) is at least 70% and no subject grade is below 50%
No — the candidate needed a weighted average of at least 80%
Cannot be determined without knowing the subject weights
No — a 68% grade in one subject automatically disqualifies the candidate
n: Section 15 only requires a weighted general average of at least 70% with no subject grade below 50%. All four grades (78, 74, 68, 82) are above 50%, and the average of 75.5% exceeds 70%, so the candidate passes. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 15 (applied computation))

q: Which body hears and decides administrative cases involving violations of R.A. No. 9266, the IRR, or the Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice, appealable to the Commission and then the Court of Appeals?
o: The Construction Industry Arbitration Commission
The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture
The Regional Trial Court, exclusively
The Department of Labor and Employment
n: Section 7(h) empowers the Board to hear and decide administrative cases involving violations, with the Board's decision appealable to the Commission and then to the Court of Appeals. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule II, Sec. 7(h))

q: Absent just cause for extension, within how many calendar days after the licensure exam must the Board submit each candidate's ratings to the Commission?
o: Forty-five (45) calendar days
Sixty (60) calendar days
Thirty (30) calendar days
Fifteen (15) calendar days
n: Section 16 requires the Board to submit the ratings to the Commission within thirty (30) calendar days after the examination, unless extended for just cause. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 16)

q: Taking Section 29 (unauthorized practice penal clause) together with Section 32 (15-year civil liability under Art. 1723 of the Civil Code), what overall distinction does the IRR draw between these two kinds of liability?
o: Section 29 applies only to foreigners, while Section 32 applies only to Filipino architects
Section 32 is a criminal penalty that replaces Section 29 entirely
There is no distinction; both sections impose identical penalties

Section 29 imposes criminal/penal liability (fines and/or imprisonment) for unauthorized practice and related offenses, while Section 32 imposes civil liability (for 15 years) on the Architect-of-record specifically for the architectural documents he/she signs and seals
n: Section 29 is a penal clause imposing fines/imprisonment for unauthorized or unlawful practice, while Section 32 addresses the Architect-of-record's civil liability (15 years, under Art. 1723 of the Civil Code) for the architectural documents signed and sealed — the IRR treats criminal/penal and civil liability as distinct tracks. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 29, Sec. 32)

q: Upon initial payment of the prescribed annual registration fee, for how many years is a Professional Identification Card issued, and what keeps it valid afterward?
o: Three (3) years, then renewal is required upon payment of annual registration fees for every three (3) years thereafter
Ten (10) years, permanently valid thereafter
One (1) year, renewable annually indefinitely without further fee
Five (5) years, renewable only once in a lifetime
n: Section 18 states the PIC is issued upon payment of the registration fee for three (3) years, and reissuance or renewal thereafter is subject to payment of the annual registration fees for another and every three (3) years. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 18)

q: Per Section 10, how is compensation and allowances fixed for the Board's chairman and members?
o: No compensation is provided; the position is strictly voluntary
Comparable to that received by the chairman and members of existing regulatory Boards under the Commission, as provided in the General Appropriations Act
A fixed honorarium set solely by the UAP
Based on a percentage of licensure examination fees collected
n: Section 10 provides that the chairman and members of the Board shall receive compensation and allowances comparable to that received by the chairman and members of existing regulatory Boards under the Commission, as provided for in the General Appropriations Act. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule II, Sec. 10)

q: The Board must prepare and keep updated what document, listing the names, places of business, and other relevant data of every registered professional architect?
o: The Standards of Professional Practice
The CPD Compliance Ledger
A Roster of Architects
The Architects' National Code
n: Section 19 requires the Board to prepare and update a roster showing the names and place of business, and other relevant data, of all registered professional architects. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 19)

q: Under the IRR's Statement of Policy, what standard is the State aiming for in Filipino architects' practice and service?
o: Restricted to local, non-competitive practice
Focused solely on cost-efficiency
Merely compliant with minimum passing grades
Excellent, qualitative, world-class and globally competitive
n: Section 2 declares the State's policy to develop competent, virtuous, productive professional architects whose standards of practice shall be excellent, qualitative, world-class and globally competitive. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 2)

q: Under Section 20(3), when may an architect lawfully sign his/her name or affix his/her seal on plans or specifications prepared under another architect's supervision?
o: Only when it clearly indicates the part or parts of the work actually performed by the signing architect
As long as the client consents
Only if the other architect is deceased
Never, under any circumstance
n: Section 20(3) makes it unlawful to sign or seal documents made under another architect's supervision unless done in a manner that clearly indicates the part or parts of the work actually performed by the signing architect. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 20(3))

q: Which choice correctly captures the IRR's definition of 'Architect'?
o: Any holder of a Bachelor of Science in Architecture degree, whether licensed or not
A person professionally and academically qualified, registered and licensed under R.A. No. 9266, holding a Certificate of Registration and Professional Identification Card
Anyone who supervises construction workers on a building site
A civil engineer who has taken continuing education units in design
n: Section 3(2) defines 'Architect' as a person professionally and academically qualified, registered and licensed under R.A. No. 9266 with a Certificate of Registration and Professional Identification Card issued by the Board/PRC. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(2))

q: Section 22 bars issuance of a Certificate of Registration and PIC to which type of person?
o: Any applicant who is over 60 years of age
Any applicant who studied architecture abroad
Any person who has falsely sworn or misrepresented himself/herself in the application, or who is convicted of a crime involving moral turpitude, or of unsound mind
Any applicant who failed the exam once before passing on a retake
n: Section 22 bars registration to any person who falsely swore or misrepresented in the application, was convicted of a crime involving moral turpitude, is guilty of immoral/dishonorable conduct, or is of unsound mind. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 22)

q: Which architect bears direct and professional responsibility and liability for a project's construction supervision?
o: Consulting Architect
Physical Planner
Architect-of-record
Architect-in-charge of construction
n: Section 3(2)(b) defines 'Architect-in-charge of construction' as the licensed architect directly and professionally responsible and liable for the construction supervision of the project. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(2)(b))

q: Section 23(e) treats which specific practice — rendering architectural services without a valid service agreement guaranteeing payment — as grounds for suspension or revocation?
o: Open solicitation of projects without a valid service agreement, or allowing oneself to be exploited without one
Refusing a project due to scheduling conflicts
Charging fees higher than the Standards of Professional Practice minimum
Sub-contracting drafting work to a licensed junior architect
n: Section 23(e) makes it a ground for suspension/revocation to have openly solicited projects by undertaking services without a valid service agreement, or to have allowed oneself to be exploited by doing so without one — both being prejudicial to the profession. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 23(e))

q: Per Section 3(25), under what condition does a Consulting Architect take on civil liability under Article 1723 of the Civil Code?
o: Only when the Architect-of-record is a foreign architect
Only if he/she attempts to or succeeds in interfering with or contravening the legal and professional functions of the Architect-of-Record
Automatically, in every project he/she consults on
Never, under any circumstance
n: The Consulting Architect assumes no civil liability under Art. 1723 of the Civil Code unless he/she attempts and/or succeeds to interfere or contravene the legal and professional functions of the Architect-of-Record; otherwise he/she assumes only the normal civil liability under the service agreement with the client. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(25))

q: Section 25 makes what a precondition before someone may practice architecture, use the title 'Architect,' or hold out as one in the Philippines?
o: Mere completion of a BS Architecture degree
Membership in any professional organization, regardless of license
Receipt of a Certificate of Registration and issuance of a Professional Identification Card from the Board
Two years of apprenticeship under any engineer
n: Section 25 states no person shall practice architecture, use the title 'Architect,' or hold out as one, unless such person has received from the Board a Certificate of Registration and been issued a Professional Identification Card. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 25)

q: Which item is explicitly listed under the 'Scope of the Practice of Architecture' in Section 3(4)?
o: Notarization of legal contracts unrelated to construction
Structural steel fabrication and welding work
Issuance of business permits by the local government
Preparation of preliminary, technical, economic and financial feasibility studies of plans, models and project promotional services
n: Section 3(4)(d) lists preparation of preliminary, technical, economic and financial feasibility studies of plans, models and project promotional services as part of the scope of the practice of architecture. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(4)(d))

q: Per Section 26 (Vested Rights), what became of architects already registered when R.A. No. 9266 took effect?
o: They are automatically registered under the new law's provisions, subject to future requirements, and their existing certificates retain full force and effect
Their prior registration is voided and must be renewed from scratch
They are downgraded to 'temporary permit' status
They must retake the licensure examination under the new law
n: Section 26 provides that all architects registered at the time R.A. No. 9266 took effect are automatically registered under its provisions, and their Certificates of Registration/PICs in good standing retain the same force and effect as though issued after the law's passage. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 26)

q: An 'Architectural Firm' under the IRR — whether a sole proprietorship, partnership, or corporation — must be registered with which agencies?
o: Only the local government unit where it operates
DTI and/or SEC, and then with the Board of Architecture and PRC
The Construction Industry Arbitration Commission (CIAC) only
Only the Bureau of Internal Revenue
n: Section 3(6) defines 'Architectural Firm' as a sole proprietorship, partnership or corporation registered with the DTI and/or SEC and then with the Board of Architecture and PRC. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(6))

q: Under Section 28, which organization develops the overall Continuing Professional Development (CPD) program for architects?
o: The Commission on Higher Education
Individual review centers
The integrated and accredited professional organization (i.e., UAP, through its CPE Council)
The Department of Trade and Industry
n: Section 28 states the integrated and accredited professional organization has the responsibility of developing a CPD program for architects, formulated by the Continuing Professional Education (CPE) Council for Architects. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 28)

q: What form must a 'Service Agreement,' as the IRR defines it, take?
o: A verbal understanding between architect and client
A document signed only by the client, without the architect's signature
An informal email exchange confirming project scope
A duly notarized written contract or equivalent public instrument stipulating the scope of services and guaranteeing compensation
n: Section 3(10) defines 'Service Agreement' as a duly notarized written contract or equivalent public instrument stipulating the scope of services and guaranteeing compensation for services rendered by a registered and licensed architect. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(10))

q: Under Section 29, what fine and prison term apply to a head of a government agency or officer of a private entity who violates Section 7(L) of R.A. No. 8981?
o: Fine of P50,000 to P500,000; imprisonment of 6 months and 1 day to 6 years
Fine of P200,000 flat; imprisonment of exactly 6 years
Fine of P100,000 to P5,000,000; imprisonment of 6 months to 6 years
No fine, imprisonment of 1 to 3 years only
n: Section 29 separately provides that heads of government agencies or officers of private entities/institutions who violate Sec. 7(L) of R.A. No. 8981 shall be punished by imprisonment of six (6) months and one (1) day to six (6) years, or a fine of P50,000 to P500,000, or both. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 29)

q: Per Board Resolution No. 3, Series of 2004, which organization is the recognized 'Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization' (IAPOA) of Philippine architects?
o: Association of Structural Engineers of the Philippines
United Architects of the Philippines, Inc. (UAP)
Philippine Contractors Accreditation Board
Philippine Institute of Architects
n: Section 40 states that pursuant to Board Resolution No. 3, Series of 2004, the United Architects of the Philippines, Inc. (UAP) is the existing integrated and accredited professional organization of registered architects, matching the IAPOA definition in Sec. 3(11). (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(11); Rule V, Sec. 40)

q: Under Section 30, someone who entices, compels, or forces a registered architect to render general practice services without first executing a written contract/service agreement is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable, upon conviction, by what?
o: A fine of P50,000 only, with mandatory imprisonment
A fine of exactly P1,000,000 with no imprisonment option
A fine of not less than P200,000, or imprisonment not exceeding six (6) years, or both
No fine; only administrative suspension of the architect's license
n: Section 30 provides that anyone who forces an architect to render services without first executing a written contract/service agreement shall, upon conviction, be fined not less than P200,000 or imprisoned for a period not exceeding six (6) years, or both. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 30)

q: 'Architectural Documents,' as the IRR defines them, are outputs only an architect may sign and seal. Which of these does the term explicitly include?
o: Environmental Compliance Certificates issued by DENR
Land title documents issued by the Registry of Deeds
Structural steel shop drawings prepared by a fabricator
Vicinity maps, site development plans, architectural program, perspective drawings, floor plans, elevations, sections, and cost estimates
n: Section 3(18) lists among 'Architectural Documents' the vicinity maps, site development plans, architectural program, perspective drawings, architectural floor plans, elevations, sections, ceiling plans, schedules, detailed drawings, technical specifications and cost estimates. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(18))

q: Per Section 32, the Architect-of-record's stamped signature, seal, PTR, PRC registration number, and IAPOA membership number on architectural plans signify assumption of Article 1723 civil liability for how many years?
o: Fifteen (15) years
Five (5) years
Ten (10) years
Twenty (20) years
n: Section 32 states that the stamped signature and seal of the Architect-of-record signify assumption of the mandated fifteen (15)-year civil liability under Article 1723 of the Civil Code. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 32)

q: How long must a 'Diversified Architectural Experience' last for an architecture graduate before he/she may sit the licensure exam?
o: Three (3) years
Two (2) years
Six (6) months
One (1) year
n: Section 3(29) defines Diversified Architectural Experience as a post-baccalaureate, pre-licensure experience of two (2) years required of a graduate prior to taking the licensure examination. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(29))

q: Per Section 33, how are drawings, specifications, and other contract documents regarded once duly signed, stamped, or sealed?
o: Government property once a building permit is issued
The property of the client automatically upon payment of fees
The intellectual property and documents of the architect, whether the object for which they were made is executed or not
Public domain material available for free copying
n: Section 33 states such documents are the intellectual property and documents of the architect, whether the object for which they are made is executed or not, and cannot be duplicated without the architect's written consent for use on other projects. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 33)

q: Under the IRR's definition of 'Ownership,' a client who commissions and owns an architectural work may use the documents only for what?
o: Selling the plans to other parties
Modifying and republishing the plans as their own design
Unlimited repetitions on any future project
Executing/implementing the work for one (1), the original, project only
n: Section 3(32) states ownership shall be confined to using the architectural documents for executing/implementing the work described therein for one (1) or the original project; it does not extend to repetitions or subsequent projects. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(32))

q: Per Section 35, within what period from R.A. No. 9266's effectivity must existing/proposed government positions that primarily require architectural services be filled only by registered and licensed architects?
o: Three (3) years
Five (5) years
One (1) year
Two (2) years
n: Section 35 provides that within three (3) years from the effectivity of R.A. No. 9266, all existing and proposed government positions primarily requiring architectural services shall be filled only by registered and licensed architects. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 35)

q: Embodied in the Architects' National Code, which document sets out all aspects of professional service, prescribes minimum basic fees, and establishes the rights and obligations of both architect and client?
o: Code of Ethical Conduct
Standards of Professional Practice
Service Agreement
Certificate of Registration
n: Section 3(39) defines 'Standards of Professional Practice' as a document in the Architects' National Code defining all aspects of professional service, prescribing minimum basic fees, and establishing the rights and obligations of the architect and the client. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(39))

q: Government architect Cruz earns P480,000 annually and is architect-of-record for a P30,000,000 government project. Applying Section 35(3)'s 1.5% incentive-pay rule, capped at 50% of annual salary, how much can Cruz actually collect upon completion?
o: P30,000 (0.1% of project cost)
P480,000 (100% of annual salary)
P240,000 (the 50%-of-annual-salary cap, since 1.5% of project cost would exceed it)
P450,000 (1.5% of the project cost, uncapped)
n: 1.5% of the P30,000,000 project cost is P450,000, but Section 35(3) caps the incentive pay at 50% of the architect's annual salary — 50% of P480,000 = P240,000. Since P450,000 exceeds the cap, Architect Cruz may only collect P240,000. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 35(3) (applied computation))

q: Which acronym refers to the government body that accredits schools offering the BS Architecture program?
o: SEC
DOLE
PDCB
CHED (Commission on Higher Education)
n: Section 3(45)(c) lists CHED as the Commission on Higher Education, the body that recognizes/accredits architecture degree programs (see also Sec. 5(b) and Sec. 13(c)). (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(45)(c))

q: Per Section 35(1), may government agencies collapse existing architect plantilla positions to recreate them as non-architect positions?
o: No — such collapsing of architect plantilla positions for that purpose is prohibited
Yes, if budget-constrained
Yes, but only in local government units
Yes, with PRC approval
n: Section 35(1) prohibits all national and local agencies, including GOCCs, from collapsing existing plantilla positions for architects for the purpose of recreating them as non-architect positions. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 35(1))

q: Per Section 4, the President selects Board members from three (3) recommendees drawn from how many nominees per position, as submitted by the integrated and accredited professional organization?
o: Three (3) nominees
Five (5) nominees
Seven (7) nominees
Ten (10) nominees
n: Section 4 specifies a list of three (3) recommendees chosen from a list of five (5) nominees for each position submitted by the integrated and accredited professional organization of architects. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule II, Sec. 4)

q: Under Section 37, what minimum share of an architectural firm's owners/shareholders/incorporators must be registered and licensed architects?
n: Section 37(b) requires that registered and licensed architects compose at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the owners, shareholders, members, incorporators, or executive officers of such an entity. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 37(b))

q: Which of these is NOT a qualification Section 5 requires of a Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture member?
o: Never having been convicted of any crime involving moral turpitude
Being a citizen and resident of the Philippines
Being an active practitioner of architecture for at least ten (10) years at the time of appointment
Holding a postgraduate doctorate degree in architecture
n: Section 5 requires citizenship/residency, a BS Architecture degree, at least 10 years of active practice with valid registration, no faculty conflict of interest, and no moral turpitude conviction — but does not require a doctorate degree. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule II, Sec. 5)

q: Before taking up duties on foreign-funded or assisted government projects in the Philippines, what must foreign nationals serving as architects/consultants secure under Section 38?
o: A special/temporary permit from the Board, subject to approval of the Commission
A civil engineering license
Membership in the Integrated Bar of the Philippines
Only a tourist visa
n: Section 38 requires foreign nationals performing architectural/consultancy services on such projects to secure a special/temporary permit from the Board, subject to approval of the Commission, before assuming their duties. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 38)

q: How long is a Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture member's term, and how many times may that member be reappointed?
o: Five (5) years, reappointable twice
Three (3) years, reappointable for one full additional term of three (3) years
Two (2) years, reappointable indefinitely
Four (4) years, non-reappointable
n: Section 6 provides that Board members hold office for a term of three (3) years and may be reappointed for one full term of three (3) years. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule II, Sec. 6)

q: Per Section 38, who must serve as architect-of-record when a foreign architect works on a Philippine project under a temporary/special permit?
o: The Board Chairman personally
No architect-of-record is required in such cases
The Filipino counterpart
The foreign architect himself/herself
n: Section 38, sub-rule 5.0, provides that the Filipino counterpart shall be the architect-of-record, with duties and responsibilities defined in a covering agreement. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 38 (sub-rule 5.0))

q: Under Section 7, unless appealed to the Commission, a Board decision in an administrative case becomes final and executory after how many days from receipt of notice of judgment?
o: Ten (10) days
Thirty (30) days
Sixty (60) days
Fifteen (15) days
n: Section 7(h) provides that a Board decision in an administrative case becomes final and executory, unless appealed to the Commission, after fifteen (15) days from receipt of notice of judgment or decision. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule II, Sec. 7(h))

q: Per Section 40, an architect duly registered with the Board automatically joins which organization, gaining its benefits and privileges upon payment of required fees and dues?
o: The integrated and accredited professional organization of architects (UAP)
The Construction Industry Arbitration Commission
The Department of Trade and Industry
The Philippine Institute of Certified Public Accountants
n: Section 40 states an architect duly registered with the Board shall automatically become a member of the integrated and accredited professional organization of architects and shall receive its benefits and privileges upon payment of required fees and dues. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule V, Sec. 40)

q: Which of these counts among the Board's enumerated powers and functions under Section 7?
o: Set national tax policy for construction materials
Prescribe and adopt the Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice
Appoint the Secretary of Justice as legal adviser
Approve business permits for architectural firms at the LGU level
n: Section 7(g) empowers the Board to prescribe and/or adopt the Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule II, Sec. 7(g))

q: Section 40(1.c) lists which of the following as a function, duty, or responsibility of the UAP as IAPOA?
o: Conducting the licensure examination itself, independent of the Board
Issuing building permits for construction projects
Nominations to vacancy of positions to the Board of Architecture (BOA)
Setting the national minimum wage for architects' draftsmen
n: Section 40(1.c)(a) lists nominations to the vacancy of positions to the BOA as one of the UAP's functions as IAPOA. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule V, Sec. 40(1.c)(a))

q: Which of these constitutes a ground for suspension or removal of a Board member under Section 9?
o: Publishing an academic paper on architecture theory
Taking an approved leave of absence
Disagreeing with a Board resolution on policy grounds
Manipulation or rigging of the architecture licensure examination results, or tampering of grades
n: Section 9(d) lists manipulation or rigging of licensure examination results, disclosure of confidential exam information, or tampering of grades as a ground for suspension or removal of a Board member. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule II, Sec. 9(d))

q: Per Section 41, how many days after publication in the Official Gazette or two major newspapers do the IRR, Code of Ethical Conduct, and Standards of Professional Practice take effect?
o: Fifteen (15) days
Thirty (30) days
Sixty (60) days
Ten (10) days
n: Section 41 provides these issuances shall be effective fifteen (15) days following their publication in the Official Gazette or in two (2) major daily newspapers of general circulation. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule V, Sec. 41)

q: After the close of each year, the Board must submit what document to the Commission, detailing its proceedings?
o: A quarterly budget request
An annual report
A licensure examination question bank
A CPD accreditation certificate
n: Section 11 requires the Board to submit an annual report to the Commission after the close of each year, detailing its proceedings and recommendations. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule II, Sec. 11)

q: Under Section 43, does R.A. No. 9266 affect or block the practice of other legally recognized professions?
o: It affects only professions related to construction
Only civil engineering is exempted from its effect
No — R.A. No. 9266 shall not be construed to affect or prevent the practice of any other legally recognized profession
Yes, it supersedes all other professional regulatory laws
n: Section 43 provides that R.A. No. 9266 shall not be construed to affect or prevent the practice of any other legally recognized profession. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule V, Sec. 43)

q: How much practical/diversified experience credit does an examination applicant get for holding a Master's Degree in Architecture from a recognized institution?
o: Six (6) months
Two (2) years (the entire requirement)
No credit at all
One (1) year
n: The proviso in Section 13(c) states that an applicant holding a Master's Degree in Architecture from a recognized school shall be credited one (1) year in his/her practical experience. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 13(c))

q: Per Section 45 (Separability Clause), what becomes of the rest of the IRR if one section or provision is struck down as unconstitutional or invalid?
o: The remainder of the IRR, or its application to other persons/circumstances, shall not be affected by such declaration
The Board must draft an entirely new IRR from scratch
The entire IRR is automatically voided
Only Rule I is voided, while the rest remains
n: Section 45 provides that if any section or provision is declared unconstitutional or invalid, the remainder of the IRR, or its application to other persons or circumstances, shall not be affected by such declaration. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule V, Sec. 45)

q: Among the documents Section 13 lists, which one is required specifically of married female applicants?
o: Architect-Mentor Affidavit
Marriage Contract in NSO Security Paper
Baccalaureate Transcript of Records
NBI Clearance
n: Section 13 lists a Marriage Contract in NSO Security Paper for married female applicants among the supporting documents. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 13)

q: Per Section 47 (Effectivity), how many days after its full publication in the Official Gazette or two major newspapers, and upon Commission approval, does the IRR of the Architecture Act of 2004 take effect?
o: Thirty (30) days
Ten (10) days
Fifteen (15) days
Twenty (20) days
n: Section 47 provides that the IRR shall be effective fifteen (15) days following its full and complete publication in the Official Gazette or in two (2) major newspapers of general circulation, upon approval by the Commission. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule V, Sec. 47)

q: Which is one of the four subject groupings Section 14 prescribes for the architecture licensure exam?
o: Real Estate Appraisal and Valuation
Business Law and Taxation
Mechanical and Electrical Engineering Codes
Structural Design, Building Materials, Methods of Construction and Utilities
n: Section 14(2) lists 'Structural Design, Building Materials, and Architectural Specifications, and Methods of Construction and Utilities' as one of the four examination subjects. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 14(2))

q: R.A. No. 9266, 'The Architecture Act of 2004,' repealed which earlier law on the practice of architecture in the Philippines?
o: R.A. No. 545, as amended, 'An Act to Regulate the Practice of Architecture in the Philippines'
The Civil Code of the Philippines
P.D. No. 1096 (the National Building Code)
The Intellectual Property Code (R.A. No. 8293)
n: The IRR's title states R.A. No. 9266 repealed for the purpose R.A. No. 545, as amended, otherwise known as 'An Act to Regulate the Practice of Architecture in the Philippines.' (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Title/Preamble)

q: Under Section 15, what weighted general average must a candidate reach to pass the licensure exam, and what is the minimum allowed grade in any single subject?
o: 80% average, no grade lower than 70%
70% average, no grade lower than 50%
65% average, no grade lower than 40%
75% average, no grade lower than 60%
n: Section 15 requires a weighted general average of seventy percent (70%), with no grade lower than fifty percent (50%) in any given subject, to pass the licensure examination. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 15)

q: Which government body holds overall administrative supervision and control over the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture?
o: The Commission on Higher Education (CHED)
The Department of Trade and Industry
The Professional Regulation Commission (PRC)
The United Architects of the Philippines
n: Section 4 describes the Board as a collegial body 'under the supervision and administrative control of the Professional Regulation Commission,' consistent with Sec. 8's provision that the Board is under the PRC's administrative supervision. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule II, Sec. 4, Sec. 8)

q: Candidate B scores an overall weighted average of 74%, but only 46% in Structural Design. Does Candidate B pass under Section 15?
o: It depends on whether the Board grants a discretionary waiver
Yes, because only the weighted average matters, not individual subject scores
Yes, because the overall average of 74% exceeds the 70% requirement
No, because a grade of 46% in one subject is below the 50% minimum-per-subject requirement, regardless of the overall average
n: Section 15 requires BOTH a 70% weighted general average AND no grade lower than 50% in any given subject. Even with a 74% average, a 46% grade in one subject fails the minimum-per-subject condition, so the candidate does not pass. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 15 (applied computation))

q: Whose guidelines govern the Board's accreditation of CPD/CPE providers, and which organization built the overarching CPD program referenced in Section 28?
o: Guidelines of the Professional Regulation Commission; program developed by the United Architects of the Philippines, Inc. through its CPE Council
No guidelines exist; each CPD provider sets its own standards
Guidelines of CHED; program developed by individual universities
Guidelines of DOLE; program developed by DTI
n: Section 28 states CPD/CPE provider accreditation by the Board is based on existing guidelines of the Professional Regulation Commission, while the overall CPD program is developed by the United Architects of the Philippines, Inc., formulated by its CPE Council for Architects. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 28)

q: Before whom must every successful examination candidate take the oath of profession before practicing architecture?
o: A notary public only
Any member of the Board, any authorized government official, or any person authorized by law to administer oaths
Only the Chairman of the PRC in person
The President of the UAP exclusively
n: Section 17 requires the oath of profession to be taken before any member of the Board, any government official authorized by the Commission, or any person authorized by law to administer oaths. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 17)

q: Per Section 6, when a Board member's seat becomes vacant mid-term, how long does the replacement serve?
o: A full new term of three (3) years, regardless of when the vacancy occurred
The position is simply left vacant until the next regular appointment cycle
Only for the unexpired portion of the term
Six (6) years, to compensate for the disruption
n: Section 6 states that any vacancy occurring within the term of a member shall be filled for the unexpired portion of the term only. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule II, Sec. 6)

q: Architect Reyes received her PIC on March 1, 2020, valid for three years under Section 18. By what month/year must she renew it to avoid a lapse?
o: March 2025
March 2021
March 2022
March 2023
n: Section 18 provides the PIC's validity/renewal cycle is three (3) years, so a card issued March 2020 would need renewal by March 2023 (2020 + 3 years). (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 18 (applied computation))

q: By what short title may the Rules and Regulations Implementing R.A. No. 9266 be cited?
o: IRR of the Architecture Act of 2004
The Architects' National Code
The Architecture Practice Code
The Philippine Architecture Charter
n: Section 1 states the Rules shall be known as the Rules and Regulations Implementing R.A. No. 9266, and for brevity may be cited as the 'IRR of the Architecture Act of 2004.' (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 1)

q: Under Section 20, what must a duly licensed architect affix — bearing his/her name, registration number, and the title 'Architect' — to all architectural plans, drawings, specifications, and contract documents?
o: A digital watermark only
The prescribed seal
A notarized affidavit
A barangay clearance
n: Section 20 requires a duly licensed architect to affix the seal prescribed by the Board, bearing the registrant's name, registration number, and title 'Architect,' on architectural plans, drawings, specifications, and contract documents. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 20)

q: Which term does the IRR define as 'the art, science or profession of planning, designing and constructing buildings in their totality,' observing utility, strength, and beauty?
o: Physical Planning
Structural Conceptualization
Architecture
Urban Design
n: Section 3(1) defines 'Architecture' as the art, science or profession of planning, designing and constructing buildings in their totality, taking into account their environment, per the principles of utility, strength and beauty. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(1))

q: Beyond his/her Certificate of Registration and PIC numbers, what other number must an architect show, per Section 21, on documents he/she signs, uses, or issues?
o: His/her voter's registration number
His/her Tax Identification Number (TIN) only
His/her Social Security System (SSS) number
The professional tax receipt (PTR) number
n: Section 21 requires the architect to indicate, in addition to the COR/PIC number and validity dates, the professional tax receipt (PTR) number issued by the City/Municipal Treasurer. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 21)

q: Which architect is 'directly and professionally responsible for the total design of the project for the client,' assuming civil liability for the signed and sealed plans, specifications, and contract documents?
o: Architect-of-record
Consulting Architect
Architect-in-charge of construction
Physical Planner
n: Section 3(2)(a) defines the 'Architect-of-record' as the licensed architect directly and professionally responsible for the total design of the project, assuming civil liability for the signed and sealed plans/specifications/contract documents. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(2)(a))

q: Which of these is a listed ground under Section 23 for suspending or revoking a Certificate of Registration/PIC?
o: Having attended fewer CPD seminars than other architects
Having signed and affixed his/her seal on plans or specifications not prepared by him/her or not executed under his/her immediate supervision
Having practiced in a province other than his/her registered address
Having taken a sabbatical leave from practice for personal reasons
n: Section 23(a) lists as a ground for suspension/revocation the signing/affixing (or permitting) of one's name or seal on plans, designs, specifications or similar documents not prepared by, or not executed under the immediate supervision of, the registrant. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 23(a))

q: What term describes a licensed architect who is academically and professionally qualified, with exceptional or recognized expertise or specialization in a branch of architecture?
o: Physical Planner
Foreign Architect
Consulting Architect
Architect-of-record
n: Section 3(2)(c)/(25) defines the 'Consulting Architect' as a registered and licensed architect who is academically and professionally qualified with exceptional or recognized expertise or specialization in a branch of architecture. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(2)(c)/(25))

q: After how many years from the revocation of a Certificate of Registration may the Board, upon application, reinstate its validity, possibly without a new examination?
o: One (1) year
Five (5) years
Ten (10) years
Two (2) years
n: Section 24 provides that the Board may, after the expiration of two (2) years from the date of revocation, and upon application for proper and sufficient reasons, reinstate the validity of a revoked Certificate of Registration. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule III, Sec. 24)

q: The 'General Practice of Architecture,' as the IRR defines it, covers planning, architectural design, structural conceptualization, and general administration/direction over building erection, enlargement, or alteration. Which statement about its coverage holds TRUE?
o: It applies regardless of whether the persons engaged in the practice are Philippine residents or have their principal office here or abroad
It applies only to architects who are residents of the Philippines
It excludes architects who direct the work as head of an office rather than performing it personally
It applies only when all duties are performed by one person alone
n: Section 3(3) explicitly states General Practice of Architecture applies regardless of whether such persons are residents of the Philippines or have their principal office/place of business here or in another territory, and regardless of whether duties are performed personally or as directing head of an office. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(3))

q: How is a foreign architect or unauthorized person who carries out architectural activities in the Philippines without authorization treated?
o: Subject only to a civil fine with no criminal liability
Engaged in the unauthorized practice of architecture and criminally liable under R.A. No. 9266
Automatically registered by reciprocity
Exempt, provided the project owner consents
n: Section 25 provides that a foreign architect or unauthorized person performing architectural activities in the Philippines shall be deemed engaged in the unauthorized practice of architecture and criminally liable under R.A. No. 9266. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 25)

q: The IRR's 'Structural Conceptualization' — conceiving, choosing, and developing the type, arrangement, and proportioning of structural elements — must give due consideration to which factors?
o: Labor union requirements and material sourcing
Color scheme, brand identity and marketing appeal
Safety, cost-effectiveness, functionality and aesthetics
Zoning classification and tax assessment only
n: Section 3(5) defines Structural Conceptualization as giving due consideration to safety, cost-effectiveness, functionality and aesthetics. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(5))

q: Under Section 27 (Reciprocity), a foreign citizen may sit the Philippine architecture licensure examination only if his/her home country meets what condition?
o: Simply has a bilateral trade agreement with the Philippines unrelated to professions
Has no architecture licensing system at all
Requires no licensing examination whatsoever for architects
Admits Filipino citizens to the practice of architecture without restriction, or allows them to practice after an exam on terms of strict and absolute equality
n: Section 27 requires proof that the foreign applicant's country either admits Filipino citizens to the practice of architecture without restriction, or allows them to practice after an examination on terms of strict and absolute equality, including recognition of prerequisite degrees. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 27)

q: In the IRR of R.A. No. 9266, the term 'Board' refers to whom?
o: The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture
The Construction Industry Arbitration Commission
The United Architects of the Philippines, Inc.
The Professional Regulation Commission
n: Section 3(8) defines 'Board' as the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(8))

q: Section 29's penal clause sets what fine and imprisonment ranges for someone convicted of practicing architecture without registration/license?
o: Fine of P500,000 to P10,000,000; imprisonment of 1 year to 10 years
Fine of P100,000 to P5,000,000; imprisonment of 6 months to 6 years
Fine of P10,000 to P100,000; imprisonment of 1 month to 1 year
Fine of P50,000 to P500,000; imprisonment of 6 months and 1 day to 6 years
n: Section 29 sets the penalty for unauthorized practice of architecture and related violations at a fine of not less than P100,000 but not more than P5,000,000, or imprisonment of not less than six (6) months nor more than six (6) years, or both, at the court's discretion. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 29)

q: Violating a Service Agreement creates civil liability under which provision, unless the violator interferes with the Architect-of-Record's or Consulting Architect's legal and professional functions?
o: Article 19 of the Labor Code
Section 29 of R.A. No. 9266
Article 1723 of the Civil Code
Section 7 of R.A. No. 8981
n: Section 3(10) states that violation of the Service Agreement is a basis for civil liability under Art. 1723 of the Civil Code, unless the violator attempts/succeeds to interfere with the Architect-of-Record's or Consulting Architect's legal and professional functions. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(10))

q: How must government or private-firm employees who aren't registered architects, but who do architectural work as part of their job, go about that work?
o: Freely, without restriction, since they are government/company employees
Only with a notarized waiver from the client
Only if they hold an engineering license instead
Only under the direct supervision of a licensed architect; otherwise it is unauthorized practice penalized under Section 29
n: Section 29 states that non-architect government/private-firm employees performing architectural work must do so under the direct supervision of a licensed architect; otherwise, it constitutes unauthorized practice penalized under Sec. 29. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 29)

q: For an existing Architecture Corporation to stay validly constituted, what minimum share of it must be registered architects, and what must happen if it falls short?
o: 75%; it must comply and register again with the SEC and the BOA
50%; it must dissolve immediately
60%; it need only submit an explanation letter
90%; it must convert into a sole proprietorship
n: Section 3(17) states that in case an existing Architecture Corporation does not comply with the 75% composition requirement, it shall comply and register again with the SEC and the BOA. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(17))

q: Under Section 31, if a person or firm has a representative or employee seek architectural work on their behalf to dodge R.A. No. 9266's registration requirements, who is deemed to have violated the law?
o: Only the person, firm, or corporation that engaged the representative
Both those represented (employer) and the representative/employee are deemed guilty
No one, since only actual construction work is penalized
Only the unlicensed representative/employee
n: Section 31 states that both those represented and the representative — the employer and the employee — shall be deemed guilty of violation of R.A. No. 9266 if they seek to avoid its provisions through such an arrangement. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 31)

q: An 'Architectural Plan,' per the IRR, is described as the representation of a lateral section for a proposed building/structure taken at what height above the finished floor?
o: 3.0 meters exactly
0.5 - 1.0 meters
1.0 - 1.5 meters
2.0 - 2.5 meters
n: Section 3(21) states that the architectural plan is the representation of a lateral section for a proposed building/structure at a height of from 1.0 to 1.5 meters above the finished floor. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule I, Sec. 3(21))

q: Under Section 32, does the Architect-of-record's civil liability extend to cover other signing professionals, such as the Architect-in-charge of construction or the Consulting Architect?
o: Yes, always, regardless of employment relationship
Yes, but only for the Consulting Architect, never the Architect-in-charge of construction
This liability rule applies only to architects employed in government, not those in private practice
No — the Architect-of-record's liability is limited to architectural documents of the project and does not extend to those other professionals' liability, unless they are under his/her direct employ
n: Section 32 clarifies that the Architect-of-record's liability is limited to architectural documents of the project and does not extend to the professional responsibility or civil liability of other signing/sealing professionals (including the AICC and Consulting Architect) unless they are under his/her direct employ; the rule applies equally to government and private-firm architects. (Source: IRR of RA 9266, Rule IV, Sec. 32)
